Hi Marta —

Following up on INV-2026-1197 (due 09/30). We’re ready to release funds as soon as your AP team confirms the preferred route and remittance reference. Attach: INV-2026-1197.pdf.

Two quick questions so we can avoid hold-ups on your side:
- Do you need the payment grossed up for any withholding (WHT) or can Novus accept net with a WHT certificate after payment?
- Preferred payment method: SEPA wire (EUR) or international ACH? If wire, please confirm beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC and the exact remittance reference to include (we’ll lock that in on our side).

We can schedule the transfer as early as 09/24 CET if that works for you — if you need a later date please flag the window.

Thanks,

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the note and the invoice. Apologies for the delay — AP wanted to confirm tax treatment before we proceed. A few items from our side:

1) Withholding: Novus is subject to 10% WHT on service invoices per our local tax regime. We can either:
   a) Receive net payment (you deduct 10%) and we will provide a WHT certificate within 10 business days, or
   b) You can gross up the payment so we receive the full invoice amount (we can calculate the gross-up if you prefer).

2) Bank details (preferred for SEPA wire):
   Beneficiary: Novus Systems S.L.
   IBAN: ES21 2100 1234 5602 0005 6789
   BIC: CAIXESBBXXX
   Remittance reference: NS-1947 / INV-1197

3) AP would prefer wire to avoid ACH reconciliation issues across the EU. I’m attaching our AP instruction sheet — it outlines the required fields for fast settlement.

If you can confirm whether Redwood will gross up or send net, we’ll queue the payment for 24-Sep morning CET. Thanks.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Finance Operations
Novus Systems
marta.ruiz@novussys.com

Attachment: Novus_AP-instructions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 12:37:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Final remittance timing + AP sync for Novus Systems invoice

Rafael / Ben —

Looping in Ben on the tax side. Given the 10% WHT ask from Novus I see two practical paths:

Option A — Net payment (fastest): Redwood pays 90% of the invoice now, Novus sends WHT certificate afterward. We’ll mark the file for reconciliation and hold the remaining 10% as an open credit until certificate arrives.

Option B — Gross-up (preferred by Novus): Redwood issues a larger wire so Novus receives the full invoice amount. This avoids credits but requires us to calculate and approve the grossed-up amount (small delay).

Tradeoffs: A is operationally simplest and keeps cash predictable for Redwood; B improves vendor experience but slightly increases near-term cash out. For a strategic customer like Novus I’d recommend B if leadership signs off.

If you want to proceed with B, I’ll ask Finance to prepare the gross-up calc and Ben can confirm tax accounting. Otherwise I’ll flag for net and set the reconciliation workflow.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
